::: {#exm-thm-odds-multiplier}
#### The treated odds from the control odds
<!-- no-figure: the example checks one product of two numbers -->

In the [six-patient trial](#exm-logistic-regression), take $\vpredvar = \tp{\paren{1, -1}}$, a control patient, and $\diffvpredvar = \tp{\paren{0, 2}}$, so that $\vpredvar' = \tp{\paren{1, 1}}$ is a treated patient. <!-- check-term-links: allow: "control" here is a trial arm, not a case-control control -->
Under the [maximum likelihood fit](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-mle), the code computes the [odds](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-odds) of recovery at both [predictor](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-input) vectors,
and the control odds times the [odds multiplier](#def-odds-multiplier) of $\diffvpredvar$. <!-- check-term-links: allow: "control" here is a trial arm, not a case-control control -->

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
# fitted odds of recovery: control (x = -1), treatment (x = +1)
wf_odds <- wf_probs / (1 - wf_probs)
c(
  odds_control = wf_odds[1],
  odds_treated = wf_odds[2],
  control_times_multiplier = wf_odds[1] * wf_multiplier
)
```

The control odds are $`r round(wf_odds[1], 4)`$, and $`r round(wf_odds[1], 4)` \times `r round(wf_multiplier, 4)` = `r round(wf_odds[1] * wf_multiplier, 4)`$ equals the treated odds, as @thm-odds-multiplier states. <!-- check-term-links: allow: "control" here is a trial arm, not a case-control control -->

:::
